info.description: Edge gateway for J'Toye OaaS multi-tenant retail platform. Routes authenticated traffic to core-java with rate limiting + circuit breakers, plus handles WhatsApp order-intake webhooks with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification.
info.title: J'Toye Edge Gateway API

post.description:
Forwards an opaque list of domain items to the Core Java
API's /api/v1/sync/batch endpoint, wrapped in a circuit
breaker so edge degrades gracefully when Core is down. The
caller must present a Keycloak JWT — the tenant_id claim
is extracted and used to scope the write.

Rate-limited per tenant AFTER authentication, keyed on the
token's tenant_id (RATE_LIMIT_TENANT_RPS / _BURST), beneath a
per-replica pre-auth valve (RATE_LIMIT_RPS / _BURST) that only
guards against floods. A 429 from either layer is
application/problem+json with type
https://jtoye.uk/errors/rate-limited and code RATE_LIMITED;
wait Retry-After seconds, then retry the same request.

Core's answer is passed through. A batch core processed is
200 with core's status (SUCCESS, PARTIAL or REJECTED),
processed_count and one result per item, in request order,
each CREATED, UPDATED or REJECTED with a stable code. A
partially refused batch is still 200: read status and
results, never the HTTP status alone. A 4xx refusal from
core (application/problem+json) is relayed verbatim: same
status, content type and body, Retry-After kept. A core
outage, an open circuit breaker or any core 5xx is the
edge's own 502.

200.description: Core processed the batch: status, processed_count and per-item results

202.description: Core accepted the batch (a core that predates per-item results; no results)

400.description: The edge's own refusal: invalid body or missing tenant_id claim (application/json). Core's batch validation refusal is relayed verbatim as application/problem+json (see CoreProblem)

401.description: The edge's own refusal: missing or malformed Bearer token (application/json). Core's refusal of an expired or invalid token is relayed verbatim as application/problem+json (see CoreProblem)

403.description: Core's refusal, relayed verbatim (application/problem+json): the token lacks catalog:write (errors/forbidden) or the caller holds no grant on the target shop (errors/shop-access-denied)

429.description: Rate limit exceeded: the caller's tenant bucket or this replica's pre-auth valve is empty. application/problem+json, type https://jtoye.uk/errors/rate-limited, code RATE_LIMITED. Wait Retry-After seconds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying (at least 1); equals retryAfterSeconds in the body

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Capacity of the bucket that refused: the per-tenant burst, or the valve's burst

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Tokens left in that bucket (always 0 on a 429)

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix epoch second at which that bucket is full again

502.description: Core API unreachable, the circuit breaker is open, or core failed (5xx); core's body is never relayed

post.description:
Accepts WhatsApp message-events, verifies the HMAC-SHA256
signature in `X-Hub-Signature-256` against
`WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`, parses the message body into an
order, resolves each product-name query to a product UUID
via the Core search endpoint, and creates an order scoped
to the vendor identified by `WHATSAPP_DEFAULT_SHOP_ID`. The
endpoint is fail-closed, and the two refusals are distinct:
an absent or invalid signature is 401, while an unset
`WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` is 503 with `Retry-After` — a known,
operator-fixable unconfigured state rather than an internal
error. Neither reads the body nor calls anything downstream.

Processing outcomes (bad payload, ambiguous product, missing
default shop, Core error) always return HTTP 200 to prevent
WhatsApp from entering its 3-day exponential retry loop.
Real error signals are in the structured logs.

This is a PUBLIC route: Meta authenticates via the HMAC
signature alone (it cannot present a Keycloak JWT). The edge
mints its own client-credentials service token for the
edge->Core call and scopes the order to WHATSAPP_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID.

parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, prefixed with 'sha256='
parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256

parameters.description: WhatsApp message-event payload (shape defined by Meta)
parameters.name: payload

429.description: This replica's pre-auth valve is empty (a per-replica flood guard, not a quota; the route is public, so no tenant bucket applies). application/problem+json, type https://jtoye.uk/errors/rate-limited, code RATE_LIMITED. Wait Retry-After seconds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying (at least 1); equals retryAfterSeconds in the body

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Tokens left in the valve (always 0 on a 429)

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix epoch second at which the valve is full again

503.description: WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET not configured — the route is unavailable until an operator sets it (fails closed)

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. This is an operator-fixable configuration state, not transient load.

get.description:
Returns 200 whenever the edge process is alive. Does not
touch any downstream dependency, so it never fails because
Core or Keycloak is having a bad day. Used by kubelet as
the liveness probe — a failing /health causes the pod to
be restarted.

Checks downstream dependencies (Core API /health + Keycloak
JWKS). Returns 503 with a per-component health map when any
dependency is unhealthy so kubelet pulls the pod out of the
Service endpoint set without restarting it.

healthy.description: Whether the downstream passed its readiness check.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.
detail.example: You have no access to this shop

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the problem type.

edge.description: Edge liveness indicator. Always "OK" when the process is up.

uptime.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at the moment the probe was served.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. RATE_LIMITED for a 429.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.
detail.example: Rate limit exceeded. Please try again in 1 seconds.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying; equals the Retry-After header.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the problem type.

type.description: Stable problem type URI. https://jtoye.uk/errors/rate-limited for a 429.

core.description: Core Java API health (via its /health endpoint).

edge.description: Edge self-status. Always "OK" when the process is up.

items.description: Opaque list of sync items. Each map is forwarded to Core as-is.

processed_count.description: Number of items written (CREATED plus UPDATED).

results.description: One result per request item, in request order.

status.description:
SUCCESS when every item was written (or the batch was empty); PARTIAL
when some were written and some rejected; REJECTED when none was
written. Never SUCCESS when any item was refused: read results.

code.description: Why the item was rejected (absent unless REJECTED).

id.description: Id of the product or shop written (absent when REJECTED).

index.description: Position of the item in the request's items array (0-based).

key.description: The item's upsert key: the sku for a product, the name for a shop.

message.description: Human-readable detail for a rejection (absent unless REJECTED).
message.example: shopId is required on every product item

accepted.description: True after receipt. Processing result is available in logs only.

BearerAuth.description: Keycloak-issued JWT. Prefix the value with `Bearer `.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization
